subject: foxes
one_liner: Skulk moves den communication out of the night air and into organized channels, so nothing has to be screamed twice.
brand_voice_notes: Sincere B2B collaboration pitch from a company that will not acknowledge its users are foxes. Every instinct is reframed as workplace jargon: screaming is async communication, scent marking is a status update, hibernation-grade avoidance is a wellness feature. Confident, HR-approved, zero winking.

hero.sub: Skulk puts every vixen, kit, and dog fox in one workspace: channels for territory, carcass logistics, and whatever that was in the hedge. Async by default, because half your team is asleep in a drainpipe.

features.title: Threaded Screaming
features.blurb: The 3 a.m. contact scream, now with replies. Keep the whole exchange in one thread instead of spread across four fields. Read receipts confirm who heard you and chose not to respond.

features.title: Scent-Synced Status
features.blurb: Mark one fence post and your availability updates across every territory you claim. Ships with Hunting, Denning, and Seen Near The Bins. No more double-marking.

features.title: Gone to Ground
features.blurb: Do-not-disturb, den-grade. Mutes every channel, huddle, and hunt for up to five months. Your team sees one word: unavailable. Compliant in most hedgerows.

demo_screen_concept: A Slack-style workspace called Hollow Farm Skulk: left sidebar with channels (#den-general, #carcass-logistics, #screaming, #henhouse-raid-q3, #sightings) and DMs whose presence indicators are paired amber 'eyeshine' dots; main pane showing threaded messages timestamped between 01:00 and 04:00; a working channel switcher; a composer that actually posts; a 'Gone to Ground' toggle that dims the whole workspace to unavailable; and a SCREAM button that posts an escalating scream to #screaming.

design_direction.style: Glassmorphic dusk-operations console, moonlit hedgerow dark mode. The page is staged as the marketing site of a heavily funded workplace-messaging company that has decided the red fox is a distributed team with an alignment problem and prices coordination by the scream. A single dusk gradient runs the full page from heather indigo (#1D1840) at the top to field-dark (#0F0C22) at the footer, one continuous night sky that is never sectioned, with a soft radial moon glow behind the hero and two or three low-opacity mist blobs drifting at different depths, so the page reads as one long field at 2 a.m. rather than a website. Every panel is true frosted glass: rgba(255,255,255,0.06) fills under backdrop-filter blur(16px), 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.14) borders, 18px radii, a faint top-edge highlight, and deep soft drop shadows; depth comes entirely from blur, layering, and border glow. No paper textures, no hairline rules as structure, no offset brutalist shadows, no clay squish. Structural labels are uppercase wide-tracked microcopy (DEN OPS, CHANNEL 03, NIGHT SHIFT) set in the body face. One fox-pelt amber carries the single primary CTA per section, the wordmark's tail accent, and every presence indicator, which the product calls eyeshine: paired amber dots that pulse like eyes catching headlights. One rationed twilight lavender handles links, secondary highlights, and the moon glow, and appears nowhere else. Sora sets the wordmark and headlines in geometric grotesque with planetarium confidence; Manrope carries plain, faintly HR-approved body copy. Every figure that pretends to be coordination telemetry (screams resolved, response latency, territories synced, tier prices) is set in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures inside inset glass wells, so it reads like an ops dashboard, not marketing. Motion is nocturnal-restrained: mist drifts on a 30s loop, eyeshine pulses on a 3s cycle, glass panels rise 8px and fade in on scroll with a 40ms stagger, the CTA glows on hover and depresses 1px on press, unread badges tick once on reveal, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No light mode, no serifs, no bento lattice, no brutalist borders, no terminal chrome, no postal motifs, no emoji. Reads like a company that files predation under 'cross-functional work' and considers the 3 a.m. scream a meeting that could have been a message.
design_direction.archetype: B2B collaboration SaaS landing: glass nav with eyeshine status dot, split hero with headline left and a tilted glass workspace preview right (the #screaming channel, unread badge at 47), three-feature glass triptych, testimonial glass cards with headshots, three-tier pricing ladder with the middle tier lifted, closing CTA band, handoff to the workspace demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Mist blobs drift on a 30s loop; eyeshine presence dots pulse on a 3s cycle; glass panels rise 8px and fade in on scroll with 40ms stagger; primary CTA glows on hover, depresses 1px on press; unread counts tick once on first reveal; all motion gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero over the moon glow: left column carries the h1 in Sora 700 at clamp(2.6rem, 6vw, 4.5rem) with 'screaming' underlined by a hand-drawn amber stroke, sub in Manrope, amber CTA plus a ghost-glass secondary ('See the demo den'). Right column is a glass workspace preview tilted -2deg: sidebar sliver with channel list, message pane showing two threaded screams and an eyeshine DM row, unread badge on #screaming reading 47.
